newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas -Down on crude, naphtha bearish.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas -Down on crude, naphtha bearish.

text.p: Light distillates fell on Monday with crude, finding little support in lacklustre trading, traders said.
"The market is very quiet -- the usual Monday -- and levels are down with crude," a trader said.
October Brent on the IPE was quoted at $18.86 per barrel, down 13 cents after its close on Friday seven cents lower at $18.99.
Singapore naphtha swaps were 5-10 cents per barrel lower, last quoted at $21.00/$21.20 for both September and October.
Japan's benchmark open-spec contract for October was however talked around $1.00 per tonne lower than November, the contango reflecting the weak prompt market.
"The contango will stay for the time being because many companies have high stocks and Asian refinery production is very good," said a South Korean trader.
"The contango will last until December and then it will widen," he said.
While demand remained lacklustre, fresh supplies were being offered in the market.
Indonesia was now offering a cargo from Cilacap, further to the prompt Dumai cargo heard offered last week, traders said.
They said a term lifter of the barrels, an Indonesia petrochemical plant, had rejected both prompt cargoes after it had already covered its monthly requirements from the Mideast.
They said Indonesian affiliates were also unwilling to take up the cargoes as there were no buyers in the market.
A Japanese trader offered two September unleaded gasoline cargoes of 95 and 92-octane at $23.00 and $22.60 per barrel, fob Singapore but failed to attract any buyers.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
